author: Jeff Malec
title: Set Phasers To 'Systematic'
text:
We had always assumed William Shatner had made a killing being the spokesperson for Priceline (now known as Booking Holdings (NASDAQ: BKNG )), with the stock being one of the best performers in the US market over the past 10 years, up about 1,900% (yeah, with a comma). Here's that price action:
Problem is (well, Shatner's problem, at least) is that Captain Kirk - who can stare down photon torpedoes and take on Klingons in hand to hand combat - sold out of his Priceline stock somewhere over there in 2002 according to a recent Wall Street Journal piece , when it was in a massive drawdown of about -96%. Who in their right mind holds on to something that loses essentially all of its value? Not even Captain Kirk, it turns out.
Problem is, if he had just set his phasers to systematic, and put a simple moving average cross-over or similar strategy to work. He would have avoided that nasty selloff during the dot com bust and (perhaps more importantly) been able to see when to get back on the Priceline train before it ran away. There were mitigating circumstances, like his contract stipulating that he couldn't cash out immediately, but still… this kind of story reminds us of the " Billionaire Investor, Millionaire Mistakes " made by Bill Ackman with Valeant.
Here's an example of how a simple 20/50 moving average system (going long only) on Priceline would have done compared with buy and hold. The systematic model holds the stock when the 20-day moving average is above the 50 day, and is flat/out of the position when the 20-day average is below the 50-day moving average. That's about as simple of a trend following strategy as you can get.
You can see that the simple model does much better than buy and hold. But, there's an interesting twist here. Say Shatner was forced to hold the stock through the dot com bust and didn't have the ability to use a systematic model to go flat (ignoring for a second that he could have created a synthetic short position via options or Nasdaq futures or a few other methods), and just used the model to regain exposure after the crash. Buy and Hold actually outperforms the model by about 2.5 to 1 since 2003, thanks in large part to any and every move lower proving to just be a head fake and not a real dip.
But we would still tell Captain Kirk to set his phasers to systematic every time. All that's needed is a quick look at the top chart, or the savings in drawdowns or volatility, or Ackman's troubles with Valeant, to tell us that systematic would allow us to sleep a little better, and to actually get to those huge gains. It's one thing to be invested in a high-flier like Priceline or Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) or Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ).
A few thousand put into those even 10 years ago is now worth hundreds of thousands, but it's quite another to be able to handle the wild swings and terrible drawdowns on the way there. Better to have faith in a model to protect against negative -99% and end up with half the gains, in our book.
